description: Direct flights observed landing at the airports that serve a place over the latest season, one row per origin and destination airport with every airline on that pair folded together. It names no airline and no price and is not a timetable or a booking: a row shows that passenger airlines' aircraft land there on that pattern, not that a seat is for sale. It covers direct flights only: when none comes from the guest's origin, say that connecting flights through other airports may exist and are not listed here. `airports` are the airports the place is served by, best first. For one place they carry `drive_minutes` and `drive_km` by car where known; for an area there is no drive time, because it differs per place (get_location_details gives it per place). `ferry` true means the drive crosses by ferry; when any airport you give has it, say once that ferries run on schedules and some are seasonal, so the guest checks the crossing before booking flights. Per flight: `from`/`from_name` the origin airport, `to` the destination, `weekdays` the days it lands, `arrivals` the landing times in local time at the destination, `km` the distance between the two airports. `year_round` true means all year; otherwise `season_start` is the first landing of the season, `season_end` the last landing if the route had stopped, and `season_end_last_year` the date it stopped the year before. A date that is absent is not known; never state one. `total_matching` counts all flights; the rows are the first `limit`, in the order of `airports`, then most flown. Which airport to fly into for a place comes from get_location_details; call this tool with `from` when the guest asks about flights from a place.

from.description: The guest's departure: the ICAO codes of every airport serving their departure city, comma-separated (resolve a city or an IATA code to ICAO yourself). Only flights from those airports are returned, by the order of `airports`, then most flown; when none match, the list is empty, never flights from another origin.

location.description: Place the guest wants to reach, as the guest says it. Resolved to a real place; if it resolves to nothing you get `location_unresolved` and no flights, never flights somewhere else.

location_id.description: Location id from an earlier search_locations or get_location_details result, used instead of `location`.

name: search_flights
title: Find Direct Flights to a Destination
